newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C Amatil says talks on extra board seat.
newsitem.headline: C-C Amatil says talks on extra board seat.

text.p: Soft drink bottler Coca-Cola Amatil said on Friday that negotiations were continuing over an extra board seat for the Philippines' San Miguel Corp as part of a tie-up between the two companies.

The signing of a final deal, due last month, has been delayed due to fine-tuning of commercial arrangements, as well the number of board seats, a C-C Amatil spokesman said. "That has been an area of negotiation since the announcement," said C-C Amatil corporate affairs spokesman Ian Brown.

The two beverage groups announced in April that C-C Amatil would acquire San Miguel's soft drink subsidiary in exchange for San Miguel taking a 25 percent stake in C-C Amatil. As part of the deal, San Miguel would gain three seats on the CC-Amatil board, which would be expanded from 12 to 15 members.
San Miguel's largest shareholder, the Presidential Commission on Good Government, later expressed reservations about the deal and called for increased board representation.
C-C Amatil at the time ruled out any increase.
Brown said the fundamental nature of the transaction remained intact, but San Miguel's board numbers were still being discussed.
"What has become a matter for negotiation...and is still moving to the point of resolution is whether it is three of 15 or four of 16," he said.
Details of the deal were to have been sent to C-C Amatil shareholders on May 20, ahead of an extraordinary general meeting to approve the tie-up.
Brown said details were now expected to be sent out around the second week of June.

C-C Amatil was trading six cents lower at A$15.40 at 1.30 p.m. (0330 GMT).
